Strategy: Merge the parents' residual-window rules: reward residuals in [28,48] by item/2, since such leftovers still fit common medium items, and penalize residuals in [6,20] by item/2, since they are too small for most items yet waste nearly a full bin. Add an item-sized bonus for exact fits, so a perfect fill outranks any near fit. Ranking changes only inside the windows or at exact fit; it may fail if future items rarely match the preserved window sizes.

```python
def priority(item, bins):
    return [-(r - item) + (item / 2 if 28 <= r - item <= 48 else 0) - (item / 2 if 6 <= r - item <= 20 else 0) + (item if r - item == 0 else 0) for r in bins]
```

Strategy: Combine parent two's penalty for awkward residuals in [8,22] with a fresh pairing rule: give 25 when the post-placement residual is within 8 of the item size, so the bin can still accept another copy of the same item. The pairing bonus takes precedence over the penalty when both apply. Ranking changes only for residuals near the item size or inside the penalized window; it may fail if items rarely repeat at similar sizes.

```python
def priority(item, bins):
    return [-(r - item) + (25 if abs(r - 2 * item) <= 8 else 0) - (15 if 8 <= r - item <= 22 and abs(r - 2 * item) > 8 else 0) for r in bins]
```

Strategy: Fuse the parents by a regime switch on the spread of feasible residuals: when max minus min is at most 40, apply parent one's triangular peak bonus around residual 35 to preserve a useful leftover; when the spread is wider, apply parent two's even-band bonus of 30 instead, since roomy bins exist elsewhere. Ranking changes inside the peak window or the even bands, by regime; it may fail if the spread threshold does not match real packing states.

```python
def priority(item, bins):
    return [-(r - item) + (30 - abs((r - item) - 35) if 25 <= r - item <= 45 and max(bins) - min(bins) <= 40 else (30 if ((r - item) // 10) % 2 == 0 and max(bins) - min(bins) > 40 else 0)) for r in bins]
```

Strategy: Merge parent one's tight-fit bonus with parent two's windows, but rescale the windows by item size: residuals up to 12 score 100 minus residual; residuals of one to two item sizes gain 20, since the bin can still take another similar item; residuals of a third to one item size lose 20, since they fit nothing similar yet waste space. Others score minus residual. Ranking changes inside the relative windows; it may fail if item sizes vary too widely.

```python
def priority(item, bins):
    return [(100 - (r - item) if r - item <= 12 else (20 - (r - item) if item <= r - item <= 2 * item else (-20 - (r - item) if 3 * (r - item) >= item and r - item < item else -(r - item)))) for r in bins]
```

Strategy: Fuse both parents into one modulated peak: inside [25,45] the bonus is 30 minus distance from 35, scaled by band parity — full value in even 10-wide bands, half value in odd bands. The peak then favors residuals near 40 over 35. Outside the window the rule is plain best fit. Ranking changes inside the window by band; it may fail if the parity modulation has no link to future item sizes.

```python
def priority(item, bins):
    return [-(r - item) + ((30 - abs((r - item) - 35)) if 25 <= r - item <= 45 and ((r - item) // 10) % 2 == 0 else ((30 - abs((r - item) - 35)) / 2 if 25 <= r - item <= 45 else 0)) for r in bins]
```

Strategy: Merge the parents' windows with an interior-preference rule: residuals in [28,48] earn 15 only when the bin is strictly interior — its residual lies between the smallest and largest feasible residuals — preserving the tightest and roomiest bins for future extreme items; residuals in [8,22] lose 15 as in parent two. Ranking changes only for interior bins inside the preserved window; it may fail if extreme bins are rarely the right choice to preserve.

```python
def priority(item, bins):
    return [-(r - item) + (15 if 28 <= r - item <= 48 and min(bins) - item < r - item and r - item < max(bins) - item else 0) - (15 if 8 <= r - item <= 22 else 0) for r in bins]
```

Strategy: Fuse the parents by re-centering the triangular peak on the item itself: residuals within 20 of the item size earn 30 minus their distance from the item, preserving bins that can take another copy; outside that zone, parent two's even-band bonus of 30 applies instead. The base is plain best fit. Ranking changes inside the pairing zone and in the even bands outside it; it may fail if items rarely repeat at similar sizes.

```python
def priority(item, bins):
    return [-(r - item) + ((30 - abs((r - item) - item)) if abs((r - item) - item) <= 20 else (30 if ((r - item) // 10) % 2 == 0 else 0)) for r in bins]
```

Strategy: Merge parent two's steep tight branch with parent one's band bonus on the loose branch: residuals up to 10 score 200 minus twice the residual, so near-exact fills dominate; looser bins score their residual plus 30 in even 10-wide bands, so among roomy bins even-band residuals beat odd-band ones of similar size. Ranking changes inside the even bands and at the tight threshold; it may fail if the band pattern among loose bins has no link to future items.

```python
def priority(item, bins):
    return [(200 - 2 * (r - item) if r - item <= 10 else ((r - item) + 30 if ((r - item) // 10) % 2 == 0 else (r - item))) for r in bins]
```

Strategy: Fuse the parents by total free space: with free space at least 300, apply parent one's gated rule — plus 20 for residuals in [28,48] only when the item is 1 modulo 3, minus 20 for residuals in [8,22]; when scarcer, apply parent two's plain rule: plus 15, minus 15 in the same windows. Ranking changes at the threshold and inside the windows; it may fail if free space does not predict when pickiness pays.

```python
def priority(item, bins):
    return [-(r - item) + (20 if 28 <= r - item <= 48 and item % 3 == 1 and sum(bins) >= 300 else (15 if 28 <= r - item <= 48 and sum(bins) < 300 else 0)) - (20 if 8 <= r - item <= 22 and sum(bins) >= 300 else (15 if 8 <= r - item <= 22 and sum(bins) < 300 else 0)) for r in bins]
```

Strategy: Merge parent one's tight-fit preference with parent two's windows, shifted one step away: residuals in [28,48] gain 15 and residuals in [8,22] lose 15, while a further 25 goes to bins just above the smallest feasible residual — within 5, not equal — preserving the single tightest bin for a future tiny item. Ranking changes inside the windows and near the minimum; it may fail if the tightest bin is rarely worth preserving.

```python
def priority(item, bins):
    return [-(r - item) + (15 if 28 <= r - item <= 48 else 0) - (15 if 8 <= r - item <= 22 else 0) + (25 if r > min(bins) and r <= min(bins) + 5 else 0) for r in bins]
```

Strategy: Merge the parents through a distribution anchor: residuals in [8,22] lose 15, while 20 goes to bins whose residual lies within 10 of the midpoint of the feasible residuals, preserving both extremes. The midpoint follows the open bins. Ranking changes near the midpoint and inside the penalty window; it may fail if the typical leftover is not useful to preserve.

```python
def priority(item, bins):
    return [-(r - item) - (15 if 8 <= r - item <= 22 else 0) + (20 if abs((r - item) - ((max(bins) + min(bins)) / 2 - item)) <= 10 else 0) for r in bins]
```

Strategy: Merge best fit with parent two's windows, split across item classes: items 1 modulo 3 gain 20 for residuals in [30,48], preserving useful leftovers; items 2 modulo 3 lose 20 for residuals in [8,22], avoiding awkward leftovers; items 0 modulo 3 use plain best fit. Each class exercises one parent term, so ranking changes inside the windows only for the matching class; it may fail if item residues carry no information about future sizes.

```python
def priority(item, bins):
    return [-(r - item) + (20 if 30 <= r - item <= 48 and item % 3 == 1 else 0) - (20 if 8 <= r - item <= 22 and item % 3 == 2 else 0) for r in bins]
```

Strategy: Merge best fit with parent two's windows, softening their hard edges into tapered shoulders: residuals in [28,48] gain 15 and residuals in [8,22] lose 15, while neighboring shoulders gain or lose 7 — residuals in [22,28) and (48,55] gain 7, residuals in [3,8) and (22,27] lose 7. The score now changes gradually near the window edges instead of jumping. Ranking changes inside the windows and shoulders; it may fail if the soft edges blur distinctions the hard windows captured.

```python
def priority(item, bins):
    return [-(r - item) + (15 if 28 <= r - item <= 48 else (7 if 22 <= r - item < 28 or 48 < r - item <= 55 else 0)) - (15 if 8 <= r - item <= 22 else (7 if 3 <= r - item < 8 or 22 < r - item <= 27 else 0)) for r in bins]
```

Strategy: Merge parent one's steep tight preference with parent two's windows over a logarithmic base: the score is minus ten times the log of one plus the residual, so differences among loose bins shrink and the windows decide there; residuals up to 10 add 150, keeping near-exact fills dominant; residuals in [28,48] add 15 and residuals in [8,22] subtract 15. Ranking changes at the tight threshold and inside the windows; it may fail if compressing loose-bin differences hides useful distinctions.

```python
def priority(item, bins):
    return [-10 * log(1 + (r - item)) + (150 if r - item <= 10 else 0) + (15 if 28 <= r - item <= 48 else 0) - (15 if 8 <= r - item <= 22 else 0) for r in bins]
```

Strategy: Fuse the parents by open-bin count: with at least 6 feasible bins, use parent one's steep shape — 200 minus twice the residual up to 10, then the residual itself; with fewer bins, use parent two's best-fit windows — minus residual plus 25 in [30,45] and minus 25 in [10,20]. Ranking changes at the count threshold and inside the windows; it may fail if the threshold does not match real packing states.

```python
def priority(item, bins):
    return [((200 - 2 * (r - item) if r - item <= 10 else (r - item)) if len(bins) >= 6 else (-(r - item) + 25 if 30 <= r - item <= 45 else (-(r - item) - 25 if 10 <= r - item <= 20 else -(r - item)))) for r in bins]
```

Strategy: Merge the parents by adding their window magnitudes where they overlap: residuals in the shared bonus window [30,42] gain 25 plus item/2, residuals in only one parent's bonus window gain that parent's amount — 25 in (42,45], item/2 in [28,30); residuals in the shared penalty window [10,20] lose 25 plus item/2, and residuals in [6,10) lose item/2. Agreement strengthens the adjustment. Ranking changes inside the windows by overlap; it may fail if adding the magnitudes overcorrects.

```python
def priority(item, bins):
    return [-(r - item) + (25 + item / 2 if 30 <= r - item <= 42 else (25 if 42 < r - item <= 45 else (item / 2 if 28 <= r - item < 30 else 0))) - ((25 + item / 2) if 10 <= r - item <= 20 else (item / 2 if 6 <= r - item < 10 else 0)) for r in bins]
```

Strategy: Merge best fit with the band rule, grading the bonus by item size: residuals in even 10-wide bands gain 30 for items under 40, and only 15 for larger items, since small items leave the residual pattern intact while large items swamp it. Odd-band residuals gain nothing. The base is plain best fit. Ranking changes in the even bands by item size; it may fail if item size does not predict when the band pattern matters.

```python
def priority(item, bins):
    return [-(r - item) + (30 if ((r - item) // 10) % 2 == 0 and item < 40 else (15 if ((r - item) // 10) % 2 == 0 else 0)) for r in bins]
```

Strategy: Merge best fit with the windows by flattening them into plateaus: residuals in [30,45] all score minus 25, as the bonus rises with the residual and cancels the best-fit slope; residuals in [10,20] all score minus 35, as the penalty falls with the residual; all other residuals score minus residual. Ties go to the earliest opened bin. Ranking changes inside the windows, which now tie; it may fail if the earliest bin is rarely best within a plateau.

```python
def priority(item, bins):
    return [-(r - item) + ((r - item) - 25 if 30 <= r - item <= 45 else 0) - (35 - (r - item) if 10 <= r - item <= 20 else 0) for r in bins]
```

Strategy: Merge parent one's item-centered pairing peak with parent two's windows: residuals within 20 of the item size earn 30 minus their distance from the item, preserving bins that can take another copy; outside that zone, residuals in [28,42] gain item/2, and residuals in [6,20] lose item/2. The pairing zone takes precedence over the windows. Ranking changes inside the pairing zone and the windows; it may fail if items rarely repeat at similar sizes.

```python
def priority(item, bins):
    return [-(r - item) + ((30 - abs((r - item) - item)) if abs((r - item) - item) <= 20 else (item / 2 if 28 <= r - item <= 42 else 0)) - (item / 2 if 6 <= r - item <= 20 else 0) for r in bins]
```

Strategy: Merge the parents by band-gating the pairing peak: residuals within 20 of the item earn 30 minus distance from the item, but only in even bands; outside the zone, even-band residuals still gain 15, odd-band ones nothing. The band thus decides whether pairing is rewarded. Ranking changes inside the pairing zone by band and in the even bands outside it; it may fail if the band pattern has no link to future items.

```python
def priority(item, bins):
    return [-(r - item) + ((30 - abs((r - item) - item)) if abs((r - item) - item) <= 20 and ((r - item) // 10) % 2 == 0 else (15 if ((r - item) // 10) % 2 == 0 else 0)) for r in bins]
```

Strategy: Merge best fit with the windows by making them parabolic: residuals in [30,45] gain 25 times one minus squared distance from 37.5 over 7.5, peaking at the center and vanishing at the edges; residuals in [10,20] lose 25 times one minus squared distance from 15 over 5, punishing the middle hardest. The adjustments are smooth instead of jumping at the edges. Ranking changes inside the curved windows; it may fail if the parabolic shape misjudges which residuals matter most.

```python
def priority(item, bins):
    return [-(r - item) + (25 * (1 - ((r - item - 37.5) / 7.5) ** 2) if 30 <= r - item <= 45 else 0) - (25 * (1 - ((r - item - 15) / 5) ** 2) if 10 <= r - item <= 20 else 0) for r in bins]
```

Strategy: Merge parent one's two-regime shape with parent two's windows, scaling the window strength by choice: residuals up to 12 score 100 minus residual and looser bins score their residual; residuals in [30,45] gain 25 when at least 5 bins are feasible but only 10 otherwise, and residuals in [10,20] lose the same graded amounts. Window adjustments matter most when many bins compete. Ranking changes inside the windows by bin count; it may fail if the count threshold rarely binds.

```python
def priority(item, bins):
    return [(100 - (r - item) if r - item <= 12 else (r - item)) + (25 if 30 <= r - item <= 45 and len(bins) >= 5 else (10 if 30 <= r - item <= 45 else 0)) - (25 if 10 <= r - item <= 20 and len(bins) >= 5 else (10 if 10 <= r - item <= 20 else 0)) for r in bins]
```

Strategy: Merge parent two's steep tight branch with parent one's anchor: residuals up to 10 score 200 minus twice the residual; looser bins score their residual, plus 20 within 10 of the feasible midpoint, minus 15 in [8,22]. The anchor follows the open bins; the penalty avoids awkward leftovers. Ranking changes near the midpoint, in the penalty window, and at the threshold; it may fail if the midpoint is not useful to preserve.

```python

```

Strategy: Merge best fit with parent two's shape, adding a boost for nearly empty bins: residuals up to 12 score 100 minus residual, so near-exact fills dominate; looser bins score their residual, plus 20 for residuals in [40,60], so nearly empty bins are preferred over moderately filled ones. The boost sits on top of the worst-fit loose branch. Ranking changes inside [40,60] and at the tight threshold; it may fail if nearly empty bins are better saved than spent.

```python
def priority(item, bins):
    return [(100 - (r - item) if r - item <= 12 else ((r - item) + 20 if 40 <= r - item <= 60 else (r - item))) for r in bins]
```

Strategy: Merge parent one's steep tight branch with parent two's windows over a square-root loose branch: residuals up to 10 score 200 minus twice the residual; looser bins score ten times the square root of the residual, compressing differences among roomy bins so the windows decide there — plus 25 in [30,45] and minus 25 in [10,20]. Ranking changes inside the windows and at the tight threshold; it may fail if compressing loose-bin differences hides useful distinctions.

```python
def priority(item, bins):
    return [(200 - 2 * (r - item) if r - item <= 10 else (10 * sqrt(r - item) + 25 if 30 <= r - item <= 45 else (10 * sqrt(r - item) - 25 if 10 <= r - item <= 20 else 10 * sqrt(r - item)))) for r in bins]
```

Strategy: Merge best fit with the band rule, flipping parity by item size: for items under 40, even-band residuals gain 30; for items of 40 or more, odd-band residuals gain 30 instead, since large items shift which leftovers are useful. Odd bands gain nothing for small items and even bands nothing for large ones. Ranking changes in the bands by item size; it may fail if item size does not predict which band parity matters.

```python
def priority(item, bins):
    return [-(r - item) + (30 if ((r - item) // 10) % 2 == 0 and item < 40 else (30 if ((r - item) // 10) % 2 == 1 and item >= 40 else 0)) for r in bins]
```

Strategy: Merge best fit with the windows by quantizing the base to steps of 5: the score is minus five times the residual rounded to the nearest five, so residuals in the same group tie and the earliest bin wins among them; residuals in [30,45] gain 25 and residuals in [10,20] lose 25. The rule is best fit at five-wide granularity. Ranking changes inside the groups and windows; it may fail if fine residual differences within a group actually matter.

```python
def priority(item, bins):
    return [-(((r - item) + 2) // 5) * 5 + (25 if 30 <= r - item <= 45 else 0) - (25 if 10 <= r - item <= 20 else 0) for r in bins]
```

Strategy: Merge the parents by taking the stronger magnitude in each window: residuals in the overlap [28,42] gain the larger of item/2 and 15, residuals in [43,48] gain 15; residuals in the overlap [8,20] lose the larger of item/2 and 15, residuals in [6,7] and [21,22] lose 15. Each window uses the bigger of the two parents' amounts where they agree. Ranking changes inside the windows by item size; it may fail if taking the maximum overstates both parents' evidence.

```python
def priority(item, bins):
    return [-(r - item) + (max(item / 2, 15) if 28 <= r - item <= 42 else (15 if 43 <= r - item <= 48 else 0)) - (max(item / 2, 15) if 8 <= r - item <= 20 else (15 if 6 <= r - item <= 7 or 21 <= r - item <= 22 else 0)) for r in bins]
```

Strategy: Merge the steep tight branch with the triangular peak as the loose rule, doubling the peak to compete with worst fit: residuals up to 10 score 200 minus twice the residual; residuals in [25,45] score 60 minus twice their distance from 35, replacing the worst-fit score there; looser bins score their residual. Ranking changes inside the peak zone and at the tight threshold; it may fail if doubling the peak overvalues the middle residuals.

```python

    return [(200 - 2 * (r - item) if r - item <= 10 else (60 - 2 * abs((r - item) - 35) if 25 <= r - item <= 45 else (r - item))) for r in bins]
```
